scope: Physical discovery algorithms, saved-point values and interpretation; exact optimizer replay and old rejected-case counts recorded separately
steps: Physical parameters are three positive energy gaps, three shared barrier excesses and two preparation temperatures; the reversible generator uses symmetric saddles and one common attempt frequency.

The numerical propagator uses a symmetric similarity transform, bath Gibbs weights, and the slow relaxation time; saved-point audit instead constructs the generator and uses direct matrix exponentials in physical time.
Both searches enforce nominal energy span <=4.76, temperature separation >=0.3 and component bounds before recording improving feasible candidates.
The nominal rate-ratio screen uses actual generator off-diagonal extremes with ceiling 850.
The robust screen bound takes the largest activation at +5% divided by the smallest barrier rate at -5%; independent corner-rate construction reproduces this conservative bound with ceiling 995.
Temperatures are perturbed relative to bath: T becomes 1+(T-1)(1+0.05s), not T(1+0.05s). Energies and barriers use multiplicative perturbations.
Initial KL above .011 brackets the largest tested target .01; the discovery score otherwise returns a positive rejection penalty.
KL contractivity permits the time-target residual Dh(.95tc)/delta-1. It checks three threshold values, not the continuous band.
Robust screening evaluates the nominal point and 16 single-coordinate perturbations. It does not cover simultaneous corners or interiors.
All 82 nominal and 71 robust-screen saved improvements have increasing evaluation indices and strictly decreasing scores; direct-exponential scores agree.
Both final saved search scores agree with direct-exponential evaluation. Historical evaluation counts and timing are recorded data, not proved by that point-value check.
Refinement begins with the second search candidate and accumulates the worst 12 of all 256 corners before each stage.
The active corner set is training evidence only; each proposed point is then evaluated on all 256 corners before acceptance.
All three saved active-corner sets, active scores, all-corner scores, acceptance decisions and final parameter identity were independently reconstructed.
The first accepted stage still fails a target: worst residual decreases from about .138016 to .036299 but remains positive.
The next two stages have negative worst-corner scores about -.00365153 and -.00365154; this gives finite corner/threshold evidence, not an interior proof.
The adversarial objective minimizes time savings over eight perturbation coordinates and log10(delta) in [-3,-2].
All three saved adversarial points lie in the declared domain, reproduce their recorded perturbed parameters and match independently recomputed hitting-time savings.
All three adversarial optimizer_success flags are false. Valid point values do not require convergence, but no converged global minimizer or exhaustive absence claim is supported.
The smallest saved adversarial saving is about .05120353437; this corroborates the displayed 5.1203 percent statement as a finite search observation.
The source explicitly separates numerical searches from the complete interval certificates; no new all-triplet-failure counterexample is claimed.
The independent checker passed 166 numerical comparisons with maximum discrepancy below 8e-13, using a declared absolute tolerance of 2e-8. These are finite floating-point cross-checks.
RUNME stale 32-lesson description corrected to 40; checker description now distinguishes original additive preservation from explicitly reviewed later technical edits.

All four advertised physical search commands replayed in isolation under Python3.9.13, NumPy1.26.4, SciPy1.13.1 and OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1; all saved numeric fields, histories, stage decisions and counters match exactly, ignoring elapsed times and one new nominal profile label.

Both earlier rejected-candidate audits replayed over 1256 perturbations each. All historical fields match exactly, including failure counts441 and50; current output additionally supplies three threshold/envelope arrays.
